title: ACT X
subtitle: The Bone Orchards
rewardRelicDesc: All friendly units gain +5 max HP — a blossom grown from a grief the orchard never finished tending.

jarvMoods: Now, past the Winter That Waited's last frostline, still carrying a snowflake that refuses to melt.
Now, the Worldmender, walking rows of bone-white trees that grew from graves nobody visits anymore.
Now, wondering what it costs a kingdom to love its own dead enough to grow an orchard for them.
Now, past the Regent's fall, learning that the Court's stored season was only ever the least of what Amarath buried.
orchardDesc: The Bone Orchards rise past the last frostline, groves grown from the kingdom's own dead, tended and beloved in equal measure.
This is not an orchard that grew by accident. It is an orchard Amarath planted on purpose, three centuries ago, so that every grave the void claimed would have something to grow into.
The garrisons here are not guarding a grove. They are guarding a grief the whole kingdom agreed to keep tending, long after anyone remembers whose grief it started as.
orchardkeeperDesc: The Orchard Keeper has tended this grove longer than any noble still standing watch, and she has never once let a grave go undefended.
She does not rule the orchard the way the Regent ruled a season. She tends it, row by row, making sure no name planted here is ever forgotten twice.

Three centuries of tending taught her one thing the Pale Court never had to teach: a grief kept long enough stops being sorrow and starts being love. She has not yet decided what the Worldmender is here to prune.
priorRunOpenings: The orchard threshold was already tended when you reached it, same as always — the grove remembers being crossed even when it doesn't remember by whom.
You knew the root-sconces' light this time. The bonewood company knew you knowing it.
The grove ledger at the threshold already had your crossing recorded. You are becoming a familiar entry in someone's tending.
The Keeper's retinue was already standing among the rows when you arrived. She does not believe in being surprised twice, either.

panels.title: THE BONE ORCHARDS
panels.text:
The orchard threshold is freshly tended — again.

intro.title: WAITED SNOWFLAKE
intro.text: The Regent's cold stood down at your back, and the snowflake she pressed into your palm has not once melted since. Past the last frostline, the road descends into groves grown from the kingdom's own dead, tended and beloved in equal measure.

intro.title: THE BONE ORCHARDS
intro.text: This is not an orchard that grew by accident. It is an orchard Amarath planted on purpose, three centuries ago, so that every grave the void claimed would have something to grow into. The garrisons here are not guarding a grove — they are guarding a grief the whole kingdom agreed to keep tending.

intro.title: THE ORCHARD KEEPER
intro.text: The Court's own gardener has tended this grove longer than any noble still standing watch, and she has never once let a grave go undefended. She does not rule the orchard. She tends it, row by row, making sure no name planted here is ever forgotten twice.

outro.title: THE KEEPER'S ACCOUNTING
outro.text: She does not fall like a soldier or a season. She simply sets down her shears, and the row she was tending stops needing her hands for the first time in three centuries. "I have tended more graves than I have grieved properly," she says, "and not one blossom in this orchard ever told me if the tending was enough. Tell the Court that, if it still remembers how to listen to anything that isn't its own grief." She presses a single blossom into your palm. It has not wilted.

outro.title: ORCHARD BLOSSOM
outro.text: It is a small thing to have cost a kingdom a grove's worth of grief — a single blossom that gives every friendly line a little more to hold. Holding it, you understand the Keeper better than her own tending ever explained her: a grief kept long enough doesn't stop being sorrow. It starts being love.

outro.title: THE VIGIL ROADS AHEAD
outro.text: Past the last tended row, the ground rises into processional highways walked for centuries to keep a vigil-rite alive. Somewhere along the vigil roads, the Pale Court's own procession is already marching to meet whatever the Worldmender brings next.

orchard-threshold.label: The Orchard Threshold
orchard-threshold.description: Where the last frostline gives way to groves grown from the kingdom's own dead.

the-root-causeway.label: The Root Causeway
the-root-causeway.description: A causeway grown through with roots thick enough to remember every grave it crosses.

the-bonewood-ramparts.label: The Bonewood Ramparts
the-bonewood-ramparts.description: A rampart line garrisoned like the grove still needs guarding — because to the Court, it does.

the-grove-ledger.label: The Grove Ledger
the-grove-ledger.description: A Court clerk tallying every grave planted against a name still owed remembrance.

eventConfig.title: The Grove Ledger
eventConfig.description: A clerk keeps the tally at a lectern grown through with roots, marking every grave against a grief three centuries deep. She does not ask why you're crossing. She only asks whether you intend to be tallied.

pools.label: Pay the ledger's toll (lose 6 HP, gain a rare card)
pools.consequence: Every grave tallied costs a little of your own grief. You receive a rare card.

pools.label: Take the clerk's grove-oil (gain 60 crystals)
pools.consequence: Oil set aside for a tending that never quite runs short. You gain 60 crystals.

pools.label: Rest at the ledger post's brazier (heal 10 HP)
pools.consequence: The brazier holds the grief back better than it has any right to. You heal 10 HP.

pools.label: Leave the ledger uncounted
pools.consequence: You leave the clerk to her tally.

the-tender-hearth.label: The Tender Hearth
the-tender-hearth.description: A garrison hearth, kept lit for grove-tenders coming off a cold row.

the-sealed-grovehouse-gate.label: The Sealed Grovehouse Gate
the-sealed-grovehouse-gate.description: A gate posting tending orders that read like they were never meant for a grove this ordinary.

eventConfig.title: The Sealed Grovehouse Gate
eventConfig.description: The writ nailed to the gate names every row in the grove and the season each is due to bloom. It is signed by the Court, countersigned by nobody the orchard has ever met, and dated the same day the vanguard crossed the Marches.

pools.label: Read the sealed grovehouse writ (lose 6 HP, gain a rare card)
pools.consequence: Every row named costs you something to read past. You receive a rare card.

pools.label: Take the grovehouse's oil cache (gain 70 crystals)
pools.consequence: A cache nobody in this orchard was ever going to collect. You gain 70 crystals.

pools.label: Rest behind the grovehouse's seals (heal 8 HP)
pools.consequence: Quieter than a tended row has any right to be. You heal 8 HP.

pools.label: Leave the writ unread
pools.consequence: Some orders are better left uncounted. You move on.

the-keeper-cart.label: The Keeper's Cart
the-keeper-cart.description: A trading cart parked in a grove that hasn't seen open trade in centuries.

the-bonewood-company.label: The Bonewood Company
the-bonewood-company.description: A file of Court soldiers holding formation among rows grown thick enough to hide them.

mem-c2act10-1.label: Memory Fragment
mem-c2act10-1.description: A founding charter of the orchard's first bonewood garrisons.

the-rooted-line.label: The Rooted Line
the-rooted-line.description: A line of soldiers who never got new orders when the orchard finally rooted around them.

the-deep-grove.label: The Deep Grove
the-deep-grove.description: Rows deep enough that even the mist stops following.

the-last-tending.label: The Last Tending
the-last-tending.description: The final row before the Keeper's own grove-house.

the-final-groveline.label: The Final Groveline
the-final-groveline.description: The last tended row before the Keeper's own ward. Someone has already trimmed it.

mem-c2act10-2.label: Memory Fragment
mem-c2act10-2.description: A grove-tender's log from the night the heartwood first sealed its own gate.

orchardkeeper-node.label: The Orchard Keeper
orchardkeeper-node.description: Three centuries of tending end here, before a gardener who decides which grief still deserves company.
bossDialogue: You crossed the Winter That Waited, Worldmender. The Regent gave you a season kept from the kingdom. I keep the kingdom's own dead, and I have tended every one of them longer than she tended her cold.
Three centuries in the void, and not one grave in this orchard went untended. The Regent decided what season deserved release. I decide which grief still deserves company.
The Court does not ask me to grow this orchard. It only asks that I keep every name in it from being forgotten twice. Let's begin.

the-inner-grove-gate.label: The Inner Grove Gate
the-inner-grove-gate.description: A second grove-gate, deeper in the orchard than any grief was ever meant to reach.

the-heartwood-corridor.label: The Heartwood Corridor
the-heartwood-corridor.description: A corridor grown through the orchard's own heartwood, older than the rows around it.

the-gilded-canopy.label: The Gilded Canopy
the-gilded-canopy.description: A canopy gilded over for a Keeper who has not received a real guest in three centuries.

the-hollow-roots.label: The Hollow Roots
the-hollow-roots.description: A root-hollow kept shrouded since the tending that named it stopped being spoken of.

the-deep-ledger.label: The Deep Ledger
the-deep-ledger.description: A ledger kept apart from the outer grove, recording graves the first ledger was never shown.

eventConfig.title: The Deep Ledger
eventConfig.description: This ledger sits behind a gate the outer clerks do not have keys to, recording graves the Court decided the first ledger should never see. Every entry is a name that was planted twice, once in error.

pools.label: Read the deep ledger (lose 6 HP, gain a rare card)
pools.consequence: A record within a record costs more to read. You receive a rare card.

pools.label: Take the clerk's deep cache (gain 70 crystals)
pools.consequence: A cache the first ledger never accounted for. You gain 70 crystals.

pools.label: Rest behind the deep gate (heal 9 HP)
pools.consequence: Quieter than a grove that keeps two ledgers has any right to be. You heal 9 HP.

pools.label: Leave the deep ledger unread
pools.consequence: Some graves are better left double-uncounted. You move on.

the-canopy-hearth.label: The Canopy Hearth
the-canopy-hearth.description: A second hearth, kept for tenders who serve a grove nobody outside ever hears of.

the-sealed-heartwood-gate.label: The Sealed Heartwood Gate
the-sealed-heartwood-gate.description: A second sealed gate, posting orders for a tending the outer grove was never told existed.

eventConfig.title: The Sealed Heartwood Gate
eventConfig.description: The writ on this gate is signed by the Keeper twice — once in the hand the outer grove knows, once in a hand nobody has seen in three hundred years. Both signatures agree on every row.

pools.label: Read the heartwood writ (lose 6 HP, gain a rare card)
pools.consequence: Two signatures cost more to read past than one. You receive a rare card.

pools.label: Take the heartwood gate's cache (gain 70 crystals)
pools.consequence: A cache nobody past the outer gate was ever going to collect. You gain 70 crystals.

pools.label: Rest behind the heartwood seals (heal 8 HP)
pools.consequence: Quieter than a twice-sealed gate has any right to be. You heal 8 HP.

pools.label: Leave the heartwood writ unread
pools.consequence: Some orders are better left twice-uncounted. You move on.

the-root-cellar-cart.label: The Root Cellar Cart
the-root-cellar-cart.description: A second trading cart, further in than the Keeper admits any cart has reason to be.

the-heartwood-company.label: The Heartwood Company
the-heartwood-company.description: A second file of Court soldiers, rooted in ground finer than anything the outer grove grows.

the-root-bound-line.label: The Root-Bound Line
the-root-bound-line.description: A line of tenders bound to the roots rather than the rows, for a rank the outer orchard never named.

the-last-heartwood.label: The Last Heartwood
the-last-heartwood.description: The final heartwood stand before the Keeper receives anyone at all.

the-final-canopy.label: The Final Canopy
the-final-canopy.description: The last canopy stand before the Keeper receives anyone at all.
